requirement.text: The website should have an African feel  but should not alienate non-Africans.  The website should use animation on pages which are describing the services  to grab the users attention and encourage them to sign up.

analysis.ethical_objective: Provide a culturally resonant website experience that reflects an African aesthetic while remaining welcoming to non-African users, and use service-page animation to attract attention and encourage sign-up.
explicit_requirements: The website should convey an African feel.
The website should not alienate non-African users.
Pages describing services should use animation.
The animation on service-description pages should grab users' attention and encourage sign-up.
supported_implications: The desired African aesthetic is constrained by inclusivity toward non-African users.
Animation is required specifically in the context of pages that describe services.
The intended outcome of service-page animation is to promote user attention and sign-up interest.
constraints: The African feel must not result in non-African users feeling alienated.
The animation requirement applies to pages describing services.
No particular visual style, animation type, or sign-up mechanism is specified.
ambiguities: What constitutes an 'African feel' is not defined.
What would count as alienating non-African users is not defined.
It is unclear whether every service-description page must contain animation or whether animation is required only where such pages are present.
The type, amount, placement, and behavior of animation are unspecified.
The meaning of 'sign up' and the relevant sign-up action are unspecified.
No measurable standard is given for grabbing attention or encouraging sign-up.
unsupported_assumptions_to_avoid: Do not assume a specific African country, region, culture, language, visual motif, color palette, imagery, or design style.
Do not assume that inclusivity requires localization, translation, cultural testing, demographic data collection, or specific accessibility measures.
Do not assume a particular animation technology, format, duration, motion style, or interaction pattern.
Do not assume animations must be present on pages other than service-description pages.
Do not assume sign-up conversion targets, analytics, or testing procedures.
Do not assume that the requirement guarantees increased sign-ups.
possible_operational_aspects: Visual content and presentation can be assessed for whether they convey the intended African feel while remaining welcoming to non-African users.
Service-description pages can be assessed for the presence of animation intended to draw attention to services and encourage sign-up.
The sign-up invitation or path associated with service content may be considered in relation to the animation's stated purpose, without prescribing a specific design or mechanism.

initial_draft.title: Inclusive African-Inspired Service Presentation
initial_draft.description: As a website user, I want an African-inspired website experience with engaging service-page animations so that I can explore the services and consider signing up.
work_items: The website shall convey an African feel while remaining welcoming to non-African users.
Pages describing services shall include animation intended to attract users' attention and encourage sign-up.

supported_by: The requirement refers to users and non-African users of the website.
criterion_support.explanation: A generic website-user role is appropriate and does not add unsupported stakeholder characteristics.

criterion_support.criterion: Goal: experience an African-inspired website with engaging animations on service pages
supported_by: The website should have an African feel.
The website should use animation on pages describing the services.
criterion_support.explanation: The goal combines the two stated website-experience requirements without prescribing a visual style or animation mechanism.

criterion_support.criterion: Reason: explore services and consider signing up
supported_by: Service-page animation is intended to grab users' attention and encourage them to sign up.
criterion_support.explanation: Exploring service information and considering sign-up are direct, immediate uses and outcomes of engaging service-description pages. The reason does not claim that sign-up will occur.

criterion_support.criterion: The website shall convey an African feel while remaining welcoming to non-African users.
supported_by: The website should have an African feel but should not alienate non-Africans.
criterion_support.explanation: “Remaining welcoming” is a faithful normalization of the constraint against alienating non-African users.

criterion_support.criterion: Pages describing services shall include animation intended to attract users' attention and encourage sign-up.
supported_by: The website should use animation on pages which are describing the services to grab the users attention and encourage them to sign up.
criterion_support.explanation: The work item preserves the page scope, animation obligation, and stated intended purpose without adding an animation type, conversion target, or sign-up mechanism.

unresolved_issues: The source does not define what constitutes an African feel, what would make the website welcoming rather than alienating to non-African users, or how the intended attention and sign-up encouragement should be assessed. This limits implementation precision and objective verification.

issues.problem: The core aesthetic and inclusivity conditions remain inherently underspecified: the source provides no criteria for an African feel or for avoiding alienation of non-African users.
issues.recommended_change: If greater implementation precision is required, obtain source-level criteria defining the intended aesthetic and inclusivity expectations; do not invent cultural motifs, styles, or assessment processes in the EUS.

issues.problem: Although the presence of animation on service-description pages can be checked, the African-feel, non-alienation, attention-grabbing, and sign-up-encouragement conditions lack defined observable or measurable standards.
issues.recommended_change: If verification at the required quality threshold is needed, obtain source-level acceptance standards for the subjective aesthetic, inclusivity, and intended animation outcomes.
